benefits: Replaces a word across a whole document in one click instead of editing each spot.
Match and replacement counters confirm exactly what changed.
Regex mode handles patterns like dates, numbers, and extra spaces.

Bulk cleanup of pasted text: fix typos, rename terms, normalise formatting.

faqs.a: Yes. Switch on 'Use regular expression' and type a pattern. For example, ' +' (space, plus) matches any run of spaces, and replacing it with a single space collapses them. Invalid patterns show an error instead of breaking anything.
Switch on 'Whole word' and 'cat' will no longer match inside 'concatenate' or 'cats'. The tool wraps your search in word boundaries (\b) so only standalone words match.
faqs.q: How do I avoid replacing 'cat' inside 'concatenate'?

faqs.a: Yes. Switch off 'Replace all' and only the first match is replaced. The replacement counter then shows 1 (or 0 if nothing matched).
faqs.q: Can I replace only the first occurrence?

faqs.a: In the replacement box, '$&' inserts the whole match and '$1', '$2' insert regex capture groups. So finding '(\d+)-(\d+)' and replacing with '$2/$1' swaps two numbers around a dash.
faqs.q: What are $1 and $& in the replacement?

faqs.a: By default the search ignores case, so 'cat' matches 'Cat' and 'CAT'. Switch on 'Case sensitive' to match the exact capitalisation you typed.
Yes. Everything runs in your browser. Nothing you paste is uploaded, stored, or seen by anyone else.

find-and-replace.formula:
1. Build the search pattern:
   plain text -> escape special characters
   regex mode -> use the pattern as typed
   whole word -> wrap in \b...\b
2. Flags: 'g' if Replace all is on; 'i' unless Case sensitive is on.
3. matches = all non-overlapping matches of the pattern in the text.
4. result = text with matches replaced by the replacement string.
   (Replace all off -> only the first match is replaced.)

Example:
  text: 'cat sat on the cat'
  find: 'cat', replace: 'dog', replace all on
  matches: 2 -> 'dog sat on the dog'
howTo: Paste your text into the main box.
Type the word or phrase to find in the Find box.
Type its replacement in the Replace box.
Tune the options: case sensitive, whole word, regex, and replace-all vs first-only.
Check the match count, then copy or download the result.
keyFacts: Find and replace swaps every occurrence of a search term with new text.
By default the search ignores letter case; a toggle makes it exact.
Whole-word mode stops 'cat' from matching inside 'concatenate'.
Regex mode treats the search box as a pattern, unlocking advanced replacements.
Replace-all mode changes every match; first-only mode changes just the first.
The tool reports how many matches were found and replaced, so nothing changes silently.

limitations: Replacements are literal text swaps - the tool does not understand meaning or grammar.
A regex that matches nothing replaces nothing; invalid patterns show an error instead.
There is no undo history: keep a copy of the original if the change matters.
Overlapping matches are not possible - regex engines consume each match before continuing.

find-and-replace.quickAnswer: Paste your text, type what to find and what to replace it with, and every match updates instantly. Options include case-sensitive search, whole-word matching (so 'cat' does not match 'concatenate'), full regular expressions, and replace-all versus first-only. The tool counts matches before replacing, so you always know what changed. For example, finding 'cat' and replacing with 'dog' in 'cat sat on the cat' gives 'dog sat on the dog' with 2 matches.
find-and-replace.tagline: Replace words and phrases across your whole text in one click.
find-and-replace.workedExample:
Input text: 'cat sat on the cat'
Find: 'cat'   Replace with: 'dog'
Options: replace all ON, case-insensitive, whole-word OFF

Step by step:
1. Search for 'cat' (case-insensitive): matches at position 0 and position 15.
2. Matches found: 2.
3. Replace each match with 'dog'.

Result: 'dog sat on the dog'
Replacements made: 2

With whole-word ON and text 'a cat concatenates':
  'cat' matches only the standalone word -> 'a dog concatenates' (1 match).
mistakes: Replacing 'cat' without whole-word matching — 'concatenate' gets mangled and your text is ruined.
Hitting replace-all without checking the match count — one typo in the Find box can wreck the whole document.
Typing regex characters like '.' or '(' with regex mode on — they match patterns, not literal text, so escape them.
Doing a case-sensitive replace on mixed-case text — 'Apple', 'apple' and 'APPLE' are three different matches.
Replacing inside code or URLs — changing 'http' to 'https' across a file can break links that only exist as http.
